I will do it the way I usually decide on my own land: start from what worked before, look at what the neighbors around Quzhou are doing, and not take big risks. I have 12 mu, and wheat-maize is still my main steady road, because grain is safer and I have well water. Cotton can still make money, but it needs more spraying and more watching, so I will not put too much land into it. This year I will keep 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 4 mu in cotton. For fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than watch the crop turn yellow later. Wheat I will feed a little heavier on nitrogen because if wheat is weak in spring, yield drops fast. Maize after wheat I will still feed well, because summer corn grows hard and fast if there is water. Cotton I will not starve either, but I will watch costs because cotton takes more pesticide money. Tillage I will keep simple: plough for cotton land, and on wheat-maize land I will use rotary or direct sowing after harvest to save time. With well irrigation, I will water wheat the most, maize a couple of times if rain is short, and cotton when it needs it. I do not like changing too much at my age, so I will mostly follow the pattern that has kept the harvest steady.
